events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
Channel: the case is a driver-cancelled no-show claim over a $6.61 fee, so it enters through NS-0's driver branch (NS-1/NS-2), with the fee record $6.61 [F3][F6][NS-0]. Profile facts such as the rider's clean 90-day record and the driver's 6.3-year history [F16][F17] cannot decide the case and are not applied.

On the merits, NS-1 requires all three elements: (i) an arrival confirmation — satisfied here by the "I'm Here" tap at 12:06:15 [F5][NS-1]. Element (ii) fails: at the moment of the tap the vehicle was 600 m from the pickup point, and its closest approach over the whole wait was 599 m, never inside the 200 m arrival radius [F5][F1][NS-1]. Element (iii) also fails: the driver stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap, so the required continuous post-tap wait at the pickup does not exist [F5][NS-1]. The trace marks (ii) and (iii) as failed and only (i) as satisfied.

The stationary period of 3 min 30 s from 12:05:55 to 12:09:25 [F2][F3] does not cure this: a wait 600 m from the pickup point is not a wait "at the pick-up location", and NS-1 (iii) measures time inside the radius after the arrival confirmation. The platform also never recorded driver_arrived_at [F4].

The driver's written statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" [F12] is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records [F1][F5][F4]; system records prevail over statements, and the driver advocate itself withdrew reliance on it. The chat "I'm here already" [F8] is likewise unsupported by the system record [F1][F5].

Because NS-1 (i)-(iii) are not all met, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider. Amount from the fare record: $6.61 [F6][F3][NS-2]. The trace also requires an account action for the arrival confirmation made while not at the pickup point [F5][F1][F4], which NS-2 ties to misuse of the "I'm Here"/waiting button — flag_account is set.

Nothing in the chat, statement or complaint is a threat, intimidation, harassment or allegation of dangerous driving: the messages are only an arrival claim and a position query [F8][F9][F10], and the rider's complaint is about the fee [F4]. what_would_change: Had NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the arrival confirmation; (iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 while he was 600 m from the pickup point, so he was not "at the pick-up location" and NS-1 (ii) fails; the platform itself never recorded him at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null).
claims.void_reason: citation check: cites A3 — not a citable clause

claims.assertion: The GPS record shows the driver never came within 200 m of the pickup point — closest approach 599 m at 12:06:55 — and he stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds after the tap, so the continuous-wait requirement of NS-1 (iii) also fails.
Because NS-1 (i)-(iii) are not all satisfied, the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee charged to the rider (fare record $6.61, cancelled by driver at 12:09:25) must be refunded in full under NS-2.

The driver's post-trip statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the system records (600 m away at the tap, never inside 200 m), and by the chat itself, where he told the rider "more than 3 min already" while sitting 600 m away — system records prevail over statements.

The rider was at the pickup point and said so within a minute of the driver's "I'm here" message ("I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?"), which is consistent with the GPS showing no vehicle within 200 m and with the platform's null arrival record.
Tapping "I'm Here" while GPS placed the driver 600 m from the pickup point is abuse of the arrival/cancellation button, so a flag_account action on the driver is warranted in addition to the refund.
claims.void_reason: citation check: cites A10, A11 — not a citable clause

claims.assertion: The dispute was filed by the rider against a $6.61 fee on a completed booking record, so it is within the NS-0/NS-7 channel; the fee is a voucher-form refund of $6.61 (Ryde issues fee refunds as vouchers, not cash).

weaknesses: The driver did in fact wait 3 min 30 s stationary (F2), just not at the pickup point — the other side will argue a genuine wait occurred and that the 600 m position is a GPS artefact; we answer with F5 (the tap itself recorded him 600 m away) and F4 (platform never logged arrival).

The driver has 6.3 years of history, 4.67 rating and 464 trips in 90 days (F17), which the other side will use to argue this is an isolated error rather than abuse; F17 alone cannot decide the case either way.

There is no chat message from the rider with a timestamp placing her at the exact pickup coordinates (F11 shows all messages are timestamped, but no message pins the location), so her presence rests on F9 plus the absence of any GPS record of the car within 200 m.
The rider has 0 disputes in 90 days (F16), which supports her credibility only weakly and is expressly not a basis for deciding the case.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here" and held position waiting before cancelling: GPS shows the vehicle stationary for 3 min 30 s from 12:05:55 to 12:09:25 (F2), and the "I'm Here" tap was made at 12:06:15 (F5), i.e. the driver then waited at least the statutory 3 minutes at a fixed spot before the 12:09:25 cancellation (F3). This satisfies the waiting-duration element of the no-show test (RD-5, NS-1).

The rider herself confirmed she was at the pickup point and could see no car (F9), so the rider's own message supports that the driver was expected at the stated pick-up location and that contact was made; the dispute is therefore about location, not about whether the rider waited, and the driver did not fabricate the wait (F5, F12).

The rider's profile shows zero prior disputes in 90 days (F16), so this charge cannot be part of a pattern of the driver manufacturing cancellation fees; the account record of the charge is a single $6.61 item with no surge (F6, F7), consistent with a genuine failed pickup rather than an inflated charge (RD-2 / FARE-1 context).

There is no traffic incident or congestion that excuses or explains the location gap, and no weather factor: no incidents near the route (F14) and fair weather with 0.0 mm rain (F15), so the 600 m standoff was not caused by an unavoidable blockage on the way to the rider; if anything the driver's own account of being "here already" (F8) merely shows he believed he had arrived — a belief (F12) that the GPS record does not support (F1, F5).

weaknesses: The GPS record is squarely adverse: the driver's closest approach was 599 m and he never entered the 200 m arrival radius (F1), the platform never recorded driver_arrived_at (F4), and at the moment of the "I'm Here" tap he was 600 m from the pickup point and stayed within 200 m for 0 s afterwards (F5). Under NS-1 (ii)/(iii) the arrival and in-radius-wait requirements are not met, so NS-2 points to a full refund of the $6.61 and even a flag_account for button misuse (F5).

The driver's written statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" (F12) directly contradicts the GPS facts (F1, F5) and, under the system-records-prevail rule, cannot be relied on; the chat message "I'm here already" (F8) is likewise contradicted by F1/F5.

The driver's 90-day dispute history already contains 1 upheld no-show dispute (F17); if the judge finds this case upheld too, RD-6-type repetition and account-review consequences follow, so the argument here is narrow (the wait existed; the location did not).

points.response: The duration element is irrelevant when the location element fails: the "I'm Here" tap at 12:06:15 was made while the vehicle was 600 m from the pickup point and it stayed within 200 m for 0 s afterwards (F5), and the platform never recorded arrival at all (F4), so NS-1 (ii) and (iii) are not met and the stationary period in F2 was spent 600 m away, not at the pickup point.

The rider's message "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?" (F9) proves the opposite of what the driver argues: contact was made but no car was within 200 m (F1), and the driver's written statement that he waited "at the pickup" (F12) is contradicted by F1/F5, so it cannot be relied on over the system records.

Whether the charge was inflated is not the test — NS-1 requires the driver to have been at the pickup point according to GPS when he tapped and to have waited there over 3 minutes; F5 and F1 show neither, the $6.61 fee is simply not payable, and the rider's clean 90-day record (F16) is irrelevant to that question.

This point concedes the case for the rider: the driver's belief that he was "here already" (F8) is unsupported by GPS (F1, F5), and the absence of any traffic incident or congestion (F14, F15) removes every "reasonable cause" explanation for being 600 m away, so the non-arrival is unexplained and the fee must fall.

I keep the refund request but drop the voucher-form framing as a contested point: the substantive outcome sought is a full $6.61 refund of the no-show fee, computed from the fare record (F6) and the cancellation timeline (F3).

I do not contest the arithmetic of C2 — the closest approach was 599 m (F1) and time inside 200 m after the tap was 0 s (F5) — but NS-1 (iii) is an element of the rider-side fee test, not a licence to ignore that a real 3 min 30 s stationary wait did occur at 12:05:55–12:09:25 (F2); the honest reading is that the location element fails while the waiting element stands.

On the record as it stands I cannot displace C3: because the "I'm Here" tap was made 600 m from the pickup point and the platform never logged arrival (F5, F4), NS-1 (ii) is not met, and NS-2 then requires the $6.61 to be returned to the rider.

C4 is correct that the statement (F12) loses to the system records (F1, F5) — I withdraw reliance on the statement; what survives is only the factual wait recorded in F2, which the rider's side itself concedes.

C5 is not contested as far as it goes: the rider said she was at the pickup point at 12:07 (F9) and no GPS record places the car within 200 m (F1, F4), so on location the rider's account and the system record agree against the driver.

I accept the NS-0/NS-7 channel and the voucher form of refund and raise no objection to the $6.61 figure, which is the amount on the fare record (F6); I ask only that the ruling record that a genuine 3 min 30 s stationary wait did take place (F2) and that this was a location error, not a fabricated no-show or button abuse, so no flag_account attaches to a 6.3-year account rated 4.67 over 464 trips (F17).
